To partially offset these challenges, revenue growth was anchored by an 18.2 percent increase in charter fees for the icebreaker Botnica, which recorded 20 more contractual days than the prior year, and a 25.0 percent rise in electricity sales revenue.
Ferry service revenue also expanded by 1.9 percent thanks to tariff indexation aligned with fuel, labour, and consumer price indices.

verified_key_information_units.information: Operational volumes declined significantly: cargo handling fell 5.0% to 6.5 million tonnes (mainly due to liquid bulk down 33.8%), passengers decreased 2.0% to 3.6 million (with the Tallinn–Helsinki route down 2.6%), and vessel calls dropped 4.8%.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Operating Volumes section pages 4-6; KPI Table page 4

candidate_sentences.text: Operational volumes contracted across key segments, contributing to margin pressure.

Cargo handling fell by 5.0 percent to 6.5 million tonnes, weighed down by a 33.8 percent drop in liquid bulk and a 4.8 percent decline in dry bulk, influenced by ongoing geopolitical tensions disrupting European shipping routes.

Passenger traffic decreased by 2.0 percent to 3.6 million, with traditional ferry routes experiencing declines due to vessel maintenance and competitive events, while cruise passenger numbers grew nearly 48 percent amid higher ship calls.
Vessel calls overall dropped by 4.8 percent.

verified_key_information_units.information: Operating expenses rose EUR 3.9 million (24.0%) in H1 2026, primarily from fuel costs up EUR 1.4 million (47.6%) due to higher prices and severe ice conditions, electricity costs up EUR 0.7 million (28.8%), and technical maintenance/repair expenses up EUR 1.2 million (80.0%).

candidate_sentences.text: The deterioration in financial performance was primarily driven by a 24.0 percent increase in operating expenses, totaling EUR 20.2 million.
Fuel costs surged by 47.6 percent to EUR 4.4 million due to elevated diesel prices and more severe winter ice conditions increasing consumption.
Electricity costs rose by 28.8 percent to EUR 3.1 million, reflecting higher market prices, increased purchase volumes, and the introduction of a new security of supply fee.

Expenses for technical maintenance and repair grew by 80.0 percent to EUR 2.8 million, as the Group did not receive the comparable insurance payout and incurred higher repair costs for the Botnica, Old City Harbour quays, and ferries.

verified_key_information_units.information: Operating profit decreased by EUR 4.7 million (25.7%) to EUR 13.6 million and profit for the period declined by EUR 4.3 million (41.7%) to EUR 6.0 million. Adjusted EBITDA fell EUR 4.0 million (13.5%) to EUR 25.8 million, mainly due to higher operating expenses, lower cargo/passenger volumes, and the absence of prior-year one-off gains (land sale profit and insurance indemnity).
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Management Report pages 4-5, 7-8; KPI Table page 4

candidate_sentences.text: Operating profit fell by 25.7 percent to EUR 13.6 million, while profit for the period dropped by 41.7 percent to EUR 6.0 million.
Adjusted EBITDA decreased by 13.5 percent to EUR 25.8 million.

These profit reductions occurred against a comparative period that benefited from non-recurring items, including an EUR 0.9 million profit from a land disposal for the Rail Baltica project and an EUR 0.9 million insurance indemnity for repair works on the icebreaker Botnica.

verified_key_information_units.information: Investments totalled EUR 3.5 million in H1 2026 (versus EUR 12.0 million in H1 2025), mainly for ferry engine replacement, upgrades to the quay at Paldiski South Harbour, and IT infrastructure. Q2 investments were EUR 2.3 million (versus EUR 8.4 million in Q2 2025).

candidate_sentences.text: Capital expenditure decreased significantly by 70.6 percent to EUR 3.5 million, focused on ferry engine replacements, quay upgrades, and IT investments.

verified_key_information_units.information: As of 30 June 2026, total assets were EUR 615.0 million (down from EUR 622.1 million), loans and borrowings were EUR 173.4 million (stable), total liabilities were EUR 247.4 million (up from EUR 241.2 million), equity was EUR 367.7 million (down from EUR 380.9 million), and cash and cash equivalents were EUR 27.6 million (down from EUR 32.0 million).
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Interim Condensed Consolidated Statement of Financial Position page 18

candidate_sentences.text: Total assets at period-end stood at EUR 615.0 million, with equity decreasing marginally by 0.3 percent to EUR 367.7 million.

verified_key_information_units.information: Significant Q2 2026 events: (a) Tallinn City Council adopted detailed plans for Terminal A and D areas; (b) Icebreaker Botnica completed a 20-day North Sea project; (c) A EUR 32 million unsecured loan agreement was signed with OP Corporate Bank; (d) Up to 485 additional Regula ferry trips were ordered for summer 2026; (e) A EUR 19.2 million dividend was paid (85% of 2025 profit).
